one_month_reasoning: Inside the window to Nov 4: (1) the Q2 FY27 report. Modine has not announced the date yet (my search found no call notice), but last year's Q2 was Oct 29 and third-party listings say ~Oct 26, so it very likely lands inside the window. It is the first continuing-operations outlook. The Q1 release promised an 'updated outlook reflecting the continuing business'. The tests are DC margin recovery from 14.8% toward 19-20%, and whether management keeps the Q1-slide promise of DC 'full-year earnings growth in excess of 85%' (DC EBITDA >= ~$397M; I model ~$350M). (2) The 8-K/A pro forma, due ~Oct 7 and still unfiled on EDGAR as of Oct 5, which fixes the post-close net debt (~$280M est.). (3) Vertiv Q3 and the hyperscaler Q3 capex guides in late October. The Nov 18 Analyst & Investor Day (new multi-year targets, confirmed by the company's Sep 14 release) falls AFTER the window, so management may hold back multi-year detail at Q2. The DC earnings guide looks stretched against Q1, but a reset was widely expected and backlog is strong, so I have no edge on the sign. I keep the distribution centred at ~$183.5 with a ~19% log-sd: the 71%/3.5 rule less a bit because the trailing vol is inflated by the July crash and the spin, with the earnings event keeping it near the rule.

Blend 60/40 = $208.3.

inputs_detail.derivation: DC growth +65%, in the low half of the 60-80% guide because Q1 was supply-constrained. DC margin: 14.8% in Q1 (Ex.99.1); management expects the DC margin back at 19-20% in Q2 (CFO Mick Lucareli, Q1 FY27 call (company transcript): "When we look at going into Q2, we would expect, right now, a lift to be back between 19% and 20%, really driven by a significant lift in the volume recovering." src 38); I assume ~19% for the year (judgment). That is deliberately BELOW the explicit Q1-slide guide of DC 'full-year earnings growth in excess of 85%' (>= $397M, which needs ~23% margins in Q2-Q4 after Q1's $51.7M). HVAC margin 16.5% (16.7% in FY26). Corporate -$80M: Q1 FY27 adjusted corporate & eliminations was -$23.0M (vs -$15.5M a year earlier), ~-$92M annualised, against -$62.6M in FY26. I take a bit less than the run-rate because TSA fees from PT offset some of it. Q1 RemainCo EBITDA was $70.3M ($51.7M + $41.6M - $23.0M), so Q2-Q4 need ~$375M.

Management's Jan-2026 target is DC +50-70% a year for two years. I use +45%, below the range, for supply/execution risk and a possible capex digestion; that matches the capex note's base case of 2027 customer AI capex +50%. DC margin 20% (judgment; FY26 reported 19.4%). HVAC +6%. Corporate -$82M, up from -$80M on inflation, per the Q1 run-rate.
DC growth decelerates to +20% as AI capex growth slows (the capex note's base case has 2028 customer capex +22%).

Peer set of 10 (supervisor's core 8: VRT, NVT, AAON, TT, JCI, CARR, LII, SPXC, plus ETN for its Boyd liquid-cooling business and CSWI for HVAC/R). I dropped HUBB as electrical-only. All forward EV/EBITDA figures use one formula, TTM EV/EBITDA / (1 + 3Y revenue CAGR), on TTM EV/EBITDA derived from filings and Oct-5 closes, with stockanalysis consensus revenue CAGRs; I dropped my round-1 +3pt margin allowance as arbitrary. That gives a median of 20.73x (range 11.3-29.46x). The EPS-CAGR divisor gives 19.74x and the average divisor 20.23x, so I treat ~20x as the reference. 16.5x is inside the range, ~18% below ~20x. The discount rests on structural features that persist through Oct-2027: (a) concentration, with one technology customer ~11% of consolidated FY26 sales per the 10-K, ~30% of DC sales if all of it is Data Centers (estimate: 0.11 x $3,181.1M FY26 sales / $1,108.2M DC sales = ~32%; the 10-K places the customer only in the Climate Solutions segment); (b) about 30% of NTM EBITDA is commercial HVAC, whose peers LII/CARR/SPXC sit at 11.3-17.9x (derived); (c) DC EBITDA margins of ~19-20% vs VRT's ~22% (TTM GAAP EBITDA $2,561.8M / revenue $11,479.6M to 2026-06-30, 10-Q XBRL); (d) the NTM window at Oct-2027 includes DC growth decelerating to ~+20% in FY29. [Citation audit 2026-10-06: peer multiples re-derived from filings (EV from 10-Q debt/cash/shares and Oct-5 closes; TTM GAAP EBITDA) and consensus growth/EPS; aggregator multiples no longer used. The chosen multiple is unchanged.]

($700M EBITDA - D&A ~$80M - interest ~$10M) x (1 - 24% normalized tax) / 54.3M shares. D&A: FY26 DC+HVAC D&A was $47.5M; I raise it for $150-200M a year of capacity capex. Interest falls after the ~$156M prepayment and as debt is paid down.

It is inside the range. bear.story: AI capex digestion, share loss (Vertiv/Trane/JCI chillers, CDU price competition) or a slip at the large technology customer (~11% of FY26 sales per the 10-K) takes DC growth to ~+15-20% in FY28 with margins stuck at ~16%, and corporate stays at ~-$90M. NTM EBITDA is ~$480M and the market de-rates MOD to an HVAC multiple of ~12x -> ~$100-120.

base.story: Q2 resets FY27 to ~$440-470M of RemainCo EBITDA (below the >85% DC-earnings promise), which the market largely expects. DC grows ~45% in FY28 at ~20% margins and the Nov 18 Investor Day targets are credible but not raised. NTM EBITDA ~$700M at 16-17x -> ~$205.

bull.story: DC delivers the top of the 50-70% target with 21%+ margins as US capacity runs clean, the Investor Day sets ambitious multi-year targets and new hyperscaler/neocloud wins dilute the concentration. NTM EBITDA ~$820M at ~20-21x (VRT/NVT-like) -> ~$295-320.

comps_summary.peer_range: Fwd P/E 14.18-29.54x (Oct-5 close / NTM consensus EPS calendarised from stockanalysis this-year and next-year estimates; JCI FY Sep-2027 = NTM). Fwd EV/EBITDA 11.3-29.46x, derived for every peer as TTM EV/EBITDA / (1 + 3Y revenue CAGR), where TTM EV/EBITDA is computed from the peer's own 10-Q/10-K (GAAP operating earnings + D&A; debt, cash, shares) and the Oct-5 close; growth is stockanalysis consensus. With the 3Y EPS-CAGR divisor the median is 19.74x, so ~20x is the reconciled reference.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 16.5x NTM EBITDA vs a 20.73x median (~20x reconciled), and 24x P/E vs a 25.93x median. Both are inside the range, ~18% and ~7% below the reference. On today's price MOD trades at ~18x NTM (Oct26-Sep27) RemainCo EBITDA (EV ~$10.0B = 53.2M x $182.91 + ~$280M net debt, on ~$555M (estimate from my FY27E/FY28E builds)), i.e. ~10% below the reconciled median.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No premium despite the highest growth in the set. The discount (~18% on EV/EBITDA, ~7% on P/E against the filings-derived medians) rests on features that persist through the horizon. (1) Concentration: per the FY26 10-K, one global technology customer was ~11% of consolidated sales (~30% of DC sales if all of it is Data Centers (estimate: 0.11 x $3,181.1M FY26 sales / $1,108.2M DC sales = ~32%; the 10-K places the customer only in the Climate Solutions segment)), and the top ten were 49%. (2) Mix: ~30% of NTM EBITDA is commercial HVAC/refrigeration, whose closest peers (LII, CARR, SPXC) trade at 11.3-17.9x EBITDA (derived). (3) Margin: DC EBITDA margins of ~19-20% at best, after 14.8% in Q1 with repeated supply-driven misses, vs VRT's ~22% TTM EBITDA margin (10-Q XBRL). (4) Horizon fade: the Oct-2027 NTM window includes FY29, when DC growth slows to ~+20%. Sell-side outperformance calls are not used.

thesis_break_reason: At ~$125 the EV is ~$6.9B (53.2M x $125 + ~$280M net debt), ~11x my FY28E EBITDA of $635M and ~15.5x FY27E. That would price DC growth stalling, margins structurally below 15% or the loss or deferral of the large technology customer (~11% of consolidated FY26 sales per the 10-K; ~30% of DC sales if all DC, an estimate) or the multi-year capacity agreement, not ordinary volatility. It is also below the pre-spin July/August lows after adjusting for the ~$14-15/share of THRM distributed.

reasoning: I valued only the remaining Climate Solutions company from recast segment data in Modine's filings: FY26 Data Centers $1.11B sales / $214.7M EBITDA, Commercial HVAC $974M / $162.4M. FY27 guidance is DC +60-80% and HVAC +5-10%. The Q1 slides also promise DC 'full-year earnings growth in excess of 85%', and the Jan-2026 deck targets DC +50-70% a year for two years. Round 2 changes after re-checking the supervisor's points in the filings. (1) Corporate cost: the Q1 FY27 release shows adjusted corporate & eliminations of -$23.0M for the quarter (vs -$15.5M a year earlier), so I raise it from -$55M to -$80M a year. That cuts FY27E RemainCo EBITDA to ~$445M (Q1 actual $70.3M) and FY28E to ~$635M. (2) Net debt: I confirmed $432.9M at Jun 30 less the ~$156M distribution = ~$277M, i.e. ~$280M, as in round 1. (3) Comps: I dropped HUBB and the +3pt margin allowance and recomputed all 10 peers on TTM/(1+3Y revenue CAGR): median 20.5x, or ~19x reconciled with the EPS-divisor result. 16.5x is now a ~13% discount, justified by 10-K concentration (one customer ~11% of consolidated sales; ~30% of DC if all DC, an estimate), the HVAC mix and DC margins below VRT. (4) Calendar: the Nov 18 Analyst & Investor Day is confirmed and sits outside the 1-month window. The Q2 date is still unannounced but very likely ~Oct 26-29. On NTM Oct-2027 EBITDA of $700M at 16.5x and EPS of $8.54 at 24x, fair value is ~$208 (+14%), down from $215; most of the upside is earnings growth, not re-rating. I am still explicitly below management's DC earnings guide because Q1 margins make the >85% promise require ~23% margins for the rest of the year. Scenarios: bear $110 (25%), base $205 (50%), bull $305 (25%). The ladder is a lognormal mixture around those (sds ~0.30/0.22/0.20) with tails fattened toward the 71% realized vol: median ~$202, P(>=183) 0.605. Research limits: www.sec.gov blocked curl, so filings were read via WebFetch, and the pro forma 8-K/A is still unfiled.
